newsitem.title: USA: BPA seeks authority to suspend fish requirements.
newsitem.headline: BPA seeks authority to suspend fish requirements.

text.p: Chances of a power outage would be reduced if dispatchers in the Northwest had authority to suspend fish-related requirements at hydroelectric dams, said the Bonneville Power Administration's (BPA) top official.

BPA administrator Randall Hardy, here to address a Congressional subcommittee hearing on a huge power outage that hit the western grid August 10, said unilateral authority is needed for dispatchers to alert dam operators to emergencies.
He noted that when the outage occurred, it was only five minutes from the time a key high-voltage power line failed until generators at the McNary hydroelectric plant tripped off.
Several other power lines had already failed, but "we clearly knew we had a problem when Keeler-Allston," a 500-kilovolt line went down, Hardy said.
The August outage was initiated when lines heavily loaded with power sagged further in the summer heat, coming close enough to trees to flash over.
But Hardy emphasized that the more substantive problem was a lack of voltage support, due to the configuration of the power system.

Faced with continued voltage support problems in northern California the day after the outage, BPA, in consultation with the National Marine Fisheries Service, suspended fish-related spill at The Dalles dam for about three days, Hardy noted.
"We might have had a third outage if we didn't," he said.
Hardy added that extensive study of which parts of the system warrant such authority as well as what actions might be taken to offset risk to endangered fish is needed.

The BPA administrator, as well as other speakers at today's hearing, stressed improved voltage support, line maintenance and manadatory compliance with reliability standards as the key elements of ensuring operation of the power grid.
Hardy noted that BPA is "severely chastened" by the August 10 events, and accepts "full responsibility for our part--which was considerable."
